items.description: Sec. 4.1 and Table 1 give no dimensions. The geometry appears only in the 'Boundary Conditions' image of Table 1. Secs. 3.1/4.5 only say the longest side is normalized to 1 mm, so the height (aspect ratio) is unknown. Sec. 4.1 calls NTopo's case only 'a similar' cantilever, so that does not fix the geometry either.
readings: L × H = 1 × 0.5 mm (2:1, like the 40×20 footprint of the 3-D cantilever in Sec. 4.2)

items.description: The 2-D supports are drawn only in the Table 1 image. Sec. 3.2.1 says fixed sides get zero displacement in all components, but its example is the 3-D x = 0 face (Fig. 2a). The text never says whether the whole short edge or only part of it is clamped in the 2-D case.
readings: whole left edge (x = 0) clamped, u_x = u_y = 0
only part of the left edge clamped (e.g., the central half of its height)

items.entity: end load on the free (right) edge
items.description: The load point is shown only in the Table 1 image. The paper uses both conventions for its other cantilevers: a 'right bottom end' load (Sec. 4.4/Table 3) and a load at the 'center of the right side' (Fig. 5, Sec. 4.5). So neither can be assumed for the 2-D case.
readings: mid-height of the free edge (y = 0.5 H)
bottom corner of the free edge (y = 0); the top corner (y = H) gives the mirror-image design

items.description: The text never states a direction for the 2-D load; only the Table 1 image shows it. The 3-D cantilever (Sec. 4.2) talks about y-displacement at the loaded section, which suggests a transverse load. Up versus down gives the same compliance-optimal design, but the line of action matters.
readings: vertical/transverse, −y (downward)
vertical/transverse, +y (upward; same layout and compliance as −y)
horizontal/axial (±x)

items.description: DMF-TONN applies the load as a traction T over an area A sampled at N_b boundary points (Eq. 5). Sec. 4.5 instead mentions 'force vector location points'. The loaded length A is never given for the 2-D example, so it could be a single nodal force (as in a grid SIMP code) or a traction over a patch of the edge.
readings: concentrated force at a single node
uniform traction over a short edge segment (about 1–3 elements, a few % of H)
uniform shear traction over the entire free edge

items.description: Force = 0.1 N and E = 1000 N/mm² are given in Sec. 4.5 'for all examples', but that paragraph sits in the 3-D additional-examples section. The 2-D baselines (Andreassen SIMP code, NTopo) were run with 'default' settings, and no out-of-plane thickness is given. Eq. (5) also leaves open whether 0.1 N is the resultant or the traction intensity T.
readings: resultant 0.1 N on a unit (1 mm) thickness, E = 1000 N/mm²
0.1 N as traction intensity T over the loaded length
unit load F = 1 with E = 1 (normalized SIMP-code units)

items.entity: 2-D elasticity model (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The text never says how the 2-D problem is modelled. Eq. (4) is written 'for 3d problems' with the 3-D Lamé constant λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)); used in 2-D, that means plane strain. A standard 2-D SIMP code is plane stress. With ν = 0.3 the effective Poisson ratio is 0.3 under plane stress but about 0.43 under plane strain, so the choice does more than rescale stiffness.
readings: plane stress, ν = 0.3 (unit thickness)
plane strain, ν = 0.3

items.entity: void / minimum stiffness in the SIMP interpolation
items.description: Sec. 3.3 gives E = E_material·ρ³ with no lower bound. The 'binary structure compliance' in Table 1 uses ρ = 0 elements, and a grid SIMP solver needs a non-zero void stiffness or minimum density, which the text does not give.
readings: E_min = 1e-9·E (modified SIMP)
ρ_min = 1e-3 (classic SIMP)
E_min = 1e-3·E

items.entity: FE/SIMP grid for the 2-D example (also used for the volume-fraction grid and the final FEA compliance)
items.description: Sec. 4.1/Table 1 give no grid size for the 2-D cantilever, while the 3-D examples state theirs. The only constraints are: the SIMP grid has more points than the 6000-point DMF-TONN batch (Sec. 4.6), and the density-filter radius is 1.5 element sizes (Sec. 4). So the physical filter radius also depends on this unknown grid.
readings: 120 × 60 elements (2:1 domain)
160 × 80 elements (2:1 domain)
200 × 100 elements (2:1 domain)
150 × 50 elements (if the domain is 3:1)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 runs the SIMP code 'with the default convergence criterion' without giving a tolerance or maximum iteration count. The only explicit criterion in the paper is for Top3D (Sec. 4.4: 200 iterations, 0.01 tolerance).
readings: stop when the max design-variable change < 0.01, no iteration cap
at most 200 iterations with a 0.01 change tolerance
fixed budget equal to DMF-TONN's 2000 iterations

items.entity: optimization iteration count n_opt for the 2-D example
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says n_opt = 2000 for this 2-D problem ('determined empirically for 2D problems'). Sec. 4.2 says 'we use n_opt = 700 for each of the presented examples in this paper'.
readings: 2000 iterations (Sec. 4.1)
700 iterations (Sec. 4.2)

locator: Sec. 4.1, the 2-D cantilever beam of Table 1
